notes.meaning: Paul begins answering questions about gifts given to believers by the Holy Spirit. He wants the church to understand where these spiritual abilities come from and how to use them wisely. Believers should never stay in the dark about how God wants them to serve.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early Christians often received these special gifts through the sacraments of baptism and confirmation.

notes.meaning: Paul reminds the Corinthians of their past life before they trusted Christ. As pagans, or people who did not know the true God, they were led blindly into worshiping silent idols made of wood and stone. Because their idols could never speak, their old religion never gave them true spiritual life or power.

Paul gives a basic rule to test whether a message really comes from God's Spirit. Anyone speaking under the power of the Holy Spirit will never curse Jesus, and no one can truly confess that Jesus is Lord unless the Holy Spirit gives them that faith. The true Spirit always points people to love and honor Jesus Christ.

Believers are given many different gifts, ministries, and ways to serve, but they all come from the one true God. The Holy Spirit gives the gifts, the Lord Jesus directs the services, and God the Father provides the power in everyone. Since the entire Trinity works together as one source, all these varied abilities belong in harmony.

The Holy Spirit shows His presence in each Christian through a specific gift. God gives these spiritual abilities for the common good, meaning they exist to help and build up the whole church family. Gifts are never handed out to let a person boast or show off.

The Holy Spirit distributes many different gifts across the church. These include speaking God's wisdom, explaining divine truths, showing extraordinary trust in God, healing the sick, working miracles, delivering God's messages, telling true spirits from false ones, and speaking or interpreting unknown languages. God gives this wide variety of abilities so that every need in the church can be met.

differ.view: Miraculous sign gifts, such as healings, miracles, and tongues, were temporary signs meant to confirm the apostles and ended when the New Testament scriptures were completed.
Gifts of healing and miracles were not restricted to the apostles and remain active in the church until Christ returns.
The gift of tongues can serve as an individual prayer language for private devotion, but in public church services it must always be interpreted.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Because the gifts are given to build up Christ's body, and that body continues through time, these spiritual ministries continue today under the guidance of church leaders.

notes.meaning: All of these different abilities are the work of the same Holy Spirit. He decides what gift to give each person according to His own wise purpose. Because God distributes the gifts as He pleases, no one has any reason to be proud or jealous.

A human body is made of many different parts, yet all those parts together make up one single living body. The church belongs to Christ in this exact same way. Believers have many different roles, but they are all united into one body under Jesus.

Every believer has been brought into this single body by the Holy Spirit. Old worldly divisions like race, background, or social rank no longer separate Christians, because all have received and drunk of the same Spirit. This shared life in the Spirit makes the church a true family.

differ.view: The baptism of the Holy Spirit happens to every believer at the moment of salvation, placing them into the body of Christ rather than being a second blessing after conversion.
This verse describes the Holy Spirit placing a new believer into the body of Christ at conversion, which is separate from the later experience where Jesus baptizes the believer in the Holy Spirit.
Believers receive the one Holy Spirit and are joined into Christ's body when they are baptized in faith.

notes.meaning: A physical body is not made of one single part, but of many different parts. In the same way, the church cannot exist if every Christian is identical. God deliberately created variety so the whole body could function.

A foot cannot claim it is not part of the body just because it is not a hand, and an ear cannot leave the body just because it is not an eye. Comparing ourselves with others does not change who we are. Christians who feel less important or less noticed still belong completely to the body of Christ.

If the whole body were only a giant eye, it would have no way to hear anything. If the whole body were only an ear, it could never smell. A body needs each sense organ to do its own job, and the church needs every kind of worker.

God Himself designed the human body and placed every single part right where He wanted it. He did the very same thing when putting the church together. Christians can be content with their place because God chose it in His great wisdom.

If all the parts were turned into one single organ, the body itself would vanish. Instead, God made many distinct members that work together as one united whole. Unity in the church does not mean everyone must be the same.

An eye cannot say to a hand that it has no need of it, and a head cannot say the same to the feet. Even the most gifted and visible leaders cannot do their work without the help of others. Every member in Christ's church needs the rest of the family.

Parts of the body that seem weaker, such as internal organs like the heart or lungs, are actually essential for life. A person can lose an arm and live, but cannot survive without hidden organs. In the church, quiet believers who serve behind the scenes are often the most vital of all.

People give extra care and clothing to parts of the body that are less presentable, while the face and hands need no covering. God put the body together so that parts lacking natural beauty receive greater attention and honor. This teaches believers to show special respect and care to members who seem less prominent.

God designed the human body this way so that its parts would never fight against each other. Instead of forming cliques or dividing, all the members are meant to have the same caring concern for one another. The church stays healthy when its people watch out for each other.

When one part of the body is injured, the whole person feels the ache and rushes to help. When one part is cared for and feels good, the whole body shares in that comfort. In the same way, Christians should hurt alongside hurting brothers and rejoice when others are honored.

Paul applies his whole picture of the human body directly to the congregation. Together, they are the body of Christ on earth, and each individual is an important member of it. Every believer has an assigned role to play in the life of the church.

God set an orderly list of callings and gifts inside the church. He placed apostles first to lead and plant churches, followed by prophets to speak His truth and teachers to instruct, along with miracles, healings, helpers for the needy, leaders to direct affairs, and various languages. All these offices exist to build up the people of God.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Listing apostles first shows that they hold the highest authority over the church, which supports the office and authority of apostolic succession.

notes.meaning: Paul asks several questions that all expect the clear answer "No." Not every Christian is called to be an apostle, a prophet, or a teacher, and not everyone is given the power to work miracles, heal, speak in tongues, or interpret. God never meant for every believer to have the exact same role.

differ.view: Speaking in tongues is the initial sign that someone has received the baptism of the Holy Spirit, even though not all believers are given the specific public gift of tongues to speak in church meetings.
Paul's question shows that tongues are not given to all Christians, meaning speaking in tongues can never be required as proof of being filled with the Holy Spirit.

notes.meaning: Paul encourages believers to desire the gifts that do the most good for others and build up the church. Then he promises to show them a far better way that must direct how every gift is used. That supreme way is the path of Christian love.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Love, or charity, is both the highest gift and the greatest virtue, giving value to all other gifts and lasting after they pass away.
